AGRISENSE AGRICULTURAL REFERENCE GUIDE 1: CROP CULTIVATION & NPK NUTRIENT REQUIREMENTS

1. RICE (Oryza sativa)
- Ideal Soil Moisture: 70-80% (flooded/semi-aquatic conditions during initial growth).
- Temperature: 20-35°C (optimal 25-30°C).
- Humidity: 80-90%.
- Soil pH: 5.5 - 6.5 (slightly acidic clay loam).
- Nutrient Profile (NPK): High Nitrogen (80-100 kg/ha), Moderate Phosphorus (40 kg/ha), Mo

Profile (NPK): High Nitrogen (80-100 kg/ha), Moderate Phosphorus (40 kg/ha), Moderate Potassium (40 kg/ha). High rainfall requirement (150-300 cm).
- Management: Maintain 2-5 cm water level during tillering stage. Apply Urea in split doses.

2. MAIZE (Zea mays)
- Ideal Soil Moisture: 50-65%.
- Temperature: 18-27°C.
- Humidity: 55-75%.
- Soil pH: 5.8 - 7.0.
- Nutrient Profile (NPK): High Nitrogen

Humidity: 55-75%.
- Soil pH: 5.8 - 7.0.
- Nutrient Profile (NPK): High Nitrogen (70-90 kg/ha), High Phosphorus (40-50 kg/ha), Potassium (40 kg/ha). Rainfall (60-110 cm).
- Management: Well-drained fertile loam soil. Avoid waterlogging during seedling stage. Top-dress with Nitrogen at knee-high stage.

6. COTTON (Gossypium hirsutum)
- Ideal Soil Moisture: 40-55%.
- Temperature: 21-30°C.
- Humidity: 40-60%.

AGRISENSE AGRICULTURAL REFERENCE GUIDE 2: PLANT DISEASE DIAGNOSIS & MANAGEMENT

1. APPLE SCAB (Venturia inaequalis)
- Symptoms: Olive-green to brown velvety spots on leaf surfaces and fruit scab lesions.
- Causes: Fungal spores overwintering in fallen leaves under high humidity and cool temperatures.
- Treatment & Prevention: Apply preventative copper or sulfur-based fungicides during green-tip st

ention: Apply preventative copper or sulfur-based fungicides during green-tip stage. Prune trees to increase canopy airflow and sunlight penetration. Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn.

2. EARLY BLIGHT (Alternaria solani - Tomato & Potato)
- Symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric rings ("target-board" pattern) starting on lower older leaves, leading to yellowing and defoliation.

3. LATE BLIGHT (Phytophthora infestans - Tomato & Potato)
- Symptoms: Water-soaked pale green or dark lesions on leaf tips, with white mold growth on underside during damp conditions. Tubers/fruits rot rapidly with foul odor.
- Causes: Oomycete pathogen thriving in cold, wet, humid weather (15-20°C with >90% humi

: Oomycete pathogen thriving in cold, wet, humid weather (15-20°C with >90% humidity). Highly destructive.
- Treatment & Prevention: Apply systemic fungicides like Metalaxyl, Dimethomorph, or Cymoxanil immediately upon early detection. Remove and burn infected foliage immediately. Use certified disease-free seeds and resistant cultivars.

4. TOMATO YELLOW LEAF CURL VIRUS (TYLCV)
- Symptoms: Severe stunting of plants, upward curling of leaf margins, interveinal chlorosis, and drastically reduced fruit yield.
- Causes: Geminivirus transmitted exclusively by the Silverleaf Whitefly (Bemisia tabaci).
- Treatment & Prevention: Control whitefly vectors using yellow sticky traps, insecticidal soaps, or neem oil sprays

itefly vectors using yellow sticky traps, insecticidal soaps, or neem oil sprays. Cover young nursery beds with fine mesh nets (50 mesh). Remove infected plants to stop virus reservoir spread.

5. CITRUS GREENING / HUANGLONGBING (Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus - Orange / Citrus)
- Symptoms: Asymmetrical blotchy mottling on leaves, yellow shoots, small lopsided bitter fruit with aborted seeds.

- Causes: Bacterial pathogen transmitted by the Asian Citrus Psyllid (Diaphorina citri).
- Treatment & Prevention: Systemic vector management using imidacloprid or thiamethoxam. Eradicate infected trees immediately. Apply balanced micronutrient foliar sprays (Zinc, Manganese, Boron) to sustain compromised trees.

- Symptoms: White to grayish powdery fungal patches on upper leaf surfaces, young stems, and buds.
- Causes: High relative humidity at night and dry warm daytime conditions.

AGRISENSE AGRICULTURAL REFERENCE GUIDE 3: SOIL MANAGEMENT, FERTILIZER & IRRIGATION BEST PRACTICES

1. SOIL MOISTURE VS AIR HUMIDITY DEFINITION
- Soil Moisture refers to the volumetric water content contained within the soil root zone (expressed as percentage % or cb tension).
- Relative Air Humidity refers to the percentage of water vapor present in the ambient atmosphere.
- Note: Soil moisture is

ntage of water vapor present in the ambient atmosphere.
- Note: Soil moisture is independent of air humidity; a field can have high air humidity (80%) during hot fog while soil moisture is critically dry (15%).

2. SOIL pH CORRECTION & NUTRIENT AVAILABILITY
- Optimal pH range for general crops: 6.0 to 7.0 (alkaline/acidic balance allows maximum availability of N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S).
- Acidic Soil Ma

dic balance allows maximum availability of N, P, K, Ca, Mg, S).
- Acidic Soil Management (pH < 5.5): Add Agricultural Lime (Calcium Carbonate / Dolomitic Lime) at 2-5 tonnes/ha to neutralize soil acidity and increase P availability.
- Alkaline Soil Management (pH > 7.8): Apply Agricultural Elemental Sulfur or Gypsum (Calcium Sulfate) and organic manure to lower pH and release locked Micronutrients

alcium Sulfate) and organic manure to lower pH and release locked Micronutrients (Iron, Zinc, Manganese).

3. FERTILIZER BALANCE (NPK MANAGEMENT)
- Nitrogen (N): Drives vegetative leaf and canopy growth. Deficiency causes overall chlorosis (yellowing) of older leaves. Excess causes weak stems and delays fruining.
- Phosphorus (P): Essential for root extension, flower initiation, and seed/fruit set

sphorus (P): Essential for root extension, flower initiation, and seed/fruit setting. Deficiency causes dark green/purplish leaf tinting and stunted root growth.
- Potassium (K): Regulates stomatal opening, water retention, carbohydrate synthesis, and disease resistance. Deficiency causes leaf tip necrosis ("marginal scorching").

4. SMART IRRIGATION SCHEDULING
- Drip Irrigation: Recommended for row crops, orchards, and vegetables. Delivers water directly to root zone with 90-95% water efficiency.
- Critical Soil Moisture Levels:
  - < 25%: Critical Drought Stress (Immediate irrigation required).
  - 30% - 45%: Low Moisture (Scheduled irrigation recommended).
  - 50% - 70%: Normal / Optimal Moisture zone.
